Level 1 · Introduction · Week 3

When This Happens

Events start code; conditionals choose what happens.

What you will learn

  • How events (like a key press or a click) start your scripts.
  • How if and if-else let a sprite choose what to do.
  • Why an if needs a forever loop to keep checking.
  • How to give kind feedback: two stars and a wish.

The big idea

Events are doorbells. A script that starts with a yellow Events hat block waits quietly. When its doorbell rings (the flag is clicked, a key is pressed, the sprite is clicked), it runs.

Conditionals ask a yes/no question. An if block runs the blocks inside it only when the answer is “yes”. An if-else block has two mouths: “yes” blocks and “no” blocks. Exactly one of them runs.

Keep checking! An if checks only once, when it runs. To keep watching, put it inside forever, like a goalkeeper who never stops watching the ball.

Exercise3.1: Arrow-Key Explorer

Make a sprite move with the arrow keys. Each key is its own doorbell.

  1. New project. From Events, drag four “when space key pressed” blocks. Click each dropdown and choose right arrow, left arrow, up arrow and down arrow.

  2. Under each, snap a Motion block: “change x by 10” (right), “change x by −10” (left), “change y by 10” (up), “change y by −10” (down).

  3. Click the stage once, then press the arrow keys. Save as explorer: you need it for 3.3!

x is left and right. y is up and down. Which key makes y bigger? (blank to fill in)

Exercise3.2: Tickle the Ghost

  1. New project. Delete the cat (right-click → delete). Choose a Sprite: pick Ghost.

  2. Build the script. The pointy “touching mouse-pointer?” block is in Sensing. For the last “say”, delete the text so the box is empty.

  3. Click the flag, then move your mouse over the ghost and away again.

Predict first: what will happen if you take away the “forever”?

Steer your explorer to the treasure!

  1. Open your explorer project (File → Load from your computer).

  2. Choose a Sprite: add a Star. Give the star this script so it waits in the top-right corner and spins:

  2. Why? Fix it! (Remember the goalkeeper.)

Done when: every time the explorer touches the star, it says “Treasure found!” and goes back to the start.

New words

event
Something that happens (a click, a key press) that starts a script.
condition
A yes/no question, like “touching edge?”.
if
Runs the blocks inside only when the condition is yes.
if-else
Runs one set of blocks for yes and another for no.
sensing
Blocks that let a sprite notice things: touching, keys, the mouse.
feedback
Comments that help someone improve their work.

Homework: When This Happens

15–20 minutes. Do Core first; Challenge and Creative are optional.

CorePet Reactions (Scratch, about 10 minutes)

Make a virtual pet that reacts to you in three different ways.

  1. Open Scratch. Delete the cat or keep it as your pet. Or click Choose a Sprite and pick any animal.

  2. Build the three scripts below. Each one has a different doorbell (event).

  3. Click the flag. Then: click the pet, press space, and move the mouse over the pet.

  4. Save as pet-reactions.

(The sound block may have a different name for your animal: just pick any sound from the dropdown.)

ChallengeFind the bug

Kai wants the pet to say “Wake up!” whenever the mouse touches it. Kai’s script is: “when green flag clicked” → “if touching mouse-pointer? then say Wake up!”. It never says “Wake up!”. Why not? How would you fix it?

CreativeTwo stars and a wish at home

Show your pet to someone at home. Ask them for two stars (two things they like) and a wish (one idea). Write them here, then try to make the wish come true!
